fields.title: Upgrading Shopware from 6.4 to 6.7: A Complete Guide
fields.summary: A step-by-step breakdown of everything you need to plan, prepare, and execute a Shopware upgrade from version 6.4 to 6.7, covering environment prep, plugin compatibility, data migration, and post-upgrade checks.
fields.content:
Upgrading Shopware from 6.4 to 6.7: A Complete Guide

---

Overview
--------

Shopware 6.7 introduced significant architectural improvements, including a move to newer Symfony and PHP minimum requirements, an overhauled Admin SDK, improvements to the flow builder, and a redesigned storefront component system. Jumping from 6.4 directly to 6.7 is possible but requires careful planning because there are two intermediate minor releases (6.5 and 6.6) that each introduced breaking changes.

This guide walks through the full process in logical stages.


1. Pre-Upgrade Assessment
--------------------------

1.1 Review the official Shopware upgrade guides
    - Read the UPGRADE.md files for each minor release in the Shopware GitHub repository:
      * shopware/platform: UPGRADE-6.5.md, UPGRADE-6.6.md, UPGRADE-6.7.md
    - Note every breaking change that affects your custom plugins, themes, or integrations.

1.2 Audit your current environment
    - Document the current PHP version (6.4 requires PHP 7.4+; 6.7 requires PHP 8.2+).
    - Document Node.js and npm/yarn versions (6.7 requires Node 18+).
    - List all installed plugins (both Shopware Store plugins and custom-built ones).
    - Check Elasticsearch/OpenSearch usage — the integration layer changed in 6.5.

1.3 Check plugin compatibility
    - Visit the Shopware Store page for each third-party plugin and confirm a 6.7-compatible version exists.
    - For custom plugins, review all deprecated APIs listed in the UPGRADE notes.
    - Prioritise fixing or replacing incompatible plugins before upgrading the core.


2. Environment Preparation
---------------------------

2.1 Upgrade PHP
    - Shopware 6.7 requires PHP 8.2 or 8.3.
    - Update your server or container image accordingly.
    - Run `php -v` to confirm the active version.
    - Update your php.ini values: memory_limit >= 512M, max_execution_time >= 60.

2.2 Upgrade Node.js
    - Shopware 6.7 requires Node.js 18 (LTS) or higher.
    - Use nvm or your package manager to install the correct version.

2.3 Upgrade the database
    - Shopware 6.7 supports MySQL 8.0+ and MariaDB 10.11+.
    - Take a full database backup before proceeding.

2.4 Set up a staging environment
    - Always perform the upgrade on a staging clone of production first.
    - Mirror your production database and files to staging.
    - Test the full upgrade process on staging before touching production.


3. Upgrading the Shopware Core
-------------------------------

Shopware recommends upgrading one minor version at a time (6.4 -> 6.5 -> 6.6 -> 6.7) rather than jumping directly. This reduces the number of issues to debug at once.

3.1 Update composer.json
    Change the shopware/platform (or individual shopware/* packages) version constraint:

    From:   "shopware/platform": "~6.4.0"
    To:     "shopware/platform": "~6.5.0"   (first step)

    Then run:
        composer update shopware/platform --with-dependencies

3.2 Run the database migrations
        php bin/console database:migrate --all
        php bin/console database:migrate-destructive --all

3.3 Clear caches and rebuild the storefront
        php bin/console cache:clear
        php bin/console theme:compile
        php bin/console assets:install

3.4 Repeat steps 3.1-3.3 for 6.6 and then 6.7
    - After confirming the site works on 6.5, repeat for 6.6 and then 6.7.


4. Plugin and Theme Updates
----------------------------

4.1 Update third-party plugins via Composer or the Admin update manager.
    - In staging, go to Extensions > My Extensions in the Admin and update all plugins.
    - Verify each plugin still works correctly after each core version step.

4.2 Update custom plugins
    - In Shopware 6.5, the `PluginBootstrap` class was simplified; remove any custom bootstrap logic that is now handled by the framework.
    - In Shopware 6.6, the Twig template inheritance was partially reworked — audit all storefront templates.
    - In Shopware 6.7, the Admin SDK moved to Vue 3; any Admin extensions using Vue 2 APIs must be migrated.
    - Update `plugin.xml` composer constraints to declare compatibility with 6.7.

4.3 Rebuild plugin assets
        php bin/console plugin:update-all
        php bin/console theme:compile


5. Data Integrity Checks
-------------------------

5.1 Verify product and category data
    - Browse key storefront pages: homepage, category listing, product detail.
    - Check that search (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch or the default DAL search) returns results.

5.2 Run the Shopware consistency check
        php bin/console dal:validate

5.3 Check scheduled tasks
        php bin/console scheduled-task:list
    - Ensure all scheduled tasks are listed and can run (`scheduled-task:run`).

5.4 Test the checkout flow end-to-end
    - Add products to cart, complete a test order, confirm order emails are sent.


6. Performance and Configuration
----------------------------------

6.1 Enable HTTP cache and review cache configuration in .env:
        SHOPWARE_HTTP_CACHE_ENABLED=1
        SHOPWARE_HTTP_DEFAULT_TTL=7200

6.2 Configure a message queue worker (required in 6.5+):
        php bin/console messenger:consume --time-limit=60
    - Set up a Supervisor or systemd service to keep the worker running continuously.

6.3 Review .env for deprecated keys removed in 6.6 and 6.7.


7. Production Cut-over
-----------------------

7.1 Schedule a maintenance window.
7.2 Put the shop in maintenance mode:
        php bin/console sales-channel:maintenance:enable --all
7.3 Take a final full backup (database + files).
7.4 Repeat the upgrade steps on production.
7.5 Run smoke tests.
7.6 Disable maintenance mode:
        php bin/console sales-channel:maintenance:disable --all


8. Post-Upgrade Checklist
--------------------------

- [ ] Storefront pages load without errors
- [ ] Admin panel accessible and functional
- [ ] All plugins active and working
- [ ] Checkout flow completes successfully
- [ ] Order confirmation emails sending
- [ ] Search (ES/OS or DAL) returning correct results
- [ ] Scheduled tasks running
- [ ] Message queue worker running
- [ ] No critical errors in var/log/
- [ ] Performance benchmarks (TTFB, page load) acceptable


9. Rollback Plan
-----------------

If critical issues are found after go-live:
1. Re-enable maintenance mode.
2. Restore the database backup taken before the cut-over.
3. Deploy the previous codebase version from your VCS tag.
4. Clear caches and bring the site back online.

Keeping a tagged Git release for your 6.4 codebase and a corresponding database dump is the fastest way to roll back.


10. Useful Resources
---------------------

- Official upgrade notes:    https://github.com/shopware/shopware/blob/trunk/UPGRADE.md
- Shopware 6.7 requirements: https://developer.shopware.com/docs/guides/installation/requirements
- Shopware CLI tool:         https://sw-cli.fos.gg/ (automates many of the steps above)
- Shopware developer docs:   https://developer.shopware.com/
